summary:
The SP category is the story of the model right now, and it's not close: R1 and R2 are both running 62% at n=175 over the last 14 days (+9.0pts over season baseline), with R3 close behind at 59% (+5.6pts). Every rating is riding a starting-pitcher edge, and R4's raw strong-play numbers back it up — 62% at 54-33 over the last 14 days, +18.0u, and now a 63% clip across its full 94-game season sample with a 7-2 run in the last week. Meanwhile bullpen_fatigue is ice cold across the board — all four ratings show a 5-game losing streak there, and R1/R2/R3 sit at just 42% (73-102) over the last 14 days. If a today's-slate pick leans on bullpen fatigue rather than the starter, treat it skeptically; if it's built on the SP signal, lean in.

Today's board is loaded with unanimous consensus calls — 13 of 15 games have all four ratings agreeing, with only WSN@LAD and MIN@CHW splitting. The strongest signal of the day is LAA @ PIT, where every rating shows its largest delta (R1 +2.71 down to R4 +2.40) on PIT, and it's an SP matchup (Ashcraft) that fits the hot category profile. CLE @ DET is nearly as clean, with CLE favored by +1.84 to +2.12 across the board behind Valdez. On the other side, BOS @ BAL is a fade spot to watch — BOS is one of the model's best "when-liked" teams all season (75%, n=48, strong 19-6 for +17.0u) but today the model unanimously has them as the underlying pick against, at -1.42 to -1.69, meaning this is BAL getting the nod, a rare spot where the profitable BOS trend and today's rating actually point away from Boston. MIL @ CIN is similar friction: MIL is 64% overall (strong 21-11, +10.0u) as a liked team, yet today's consensus is against them by -1.17 to -2.00 across all four ratings — a legitimate fade of a normally strong team, and worth trusting given how uniform the delta is. TBR @ TEX is milder (TEX leans, all positive but under +1.0), consistent with a lower-conviction system agreement rather than a standout target.
